the application of a new method of measuring retroviral removal by Protein A chromatography.
the development of a novel, alternative, and more practical approach to measuring endogenous retroviral clearance during the production of recombinant biopharmaceutical proteins.

the protein A chromatography step is a robust and efficient CHO‐retrovirus removal step, that can be measured directly by Q‐PCR assays in the process, and that the clearance values are not impacted by a number of different operating conditions, including load density and flow rate.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a novel Q‐PCR based assay was developed and applied to measure endogenous retrovirus clearance by Protein A chromatography.
we developed a novel, Q‐PCR based approach to measuring endogenous retroviral clearance in the protein A chromatography process.

a Q‐PCR assay for measuring endogenous retroviruses in CHO cell harvests and protein pools was developed, validated, and used to measure CHO retrovirus in protein A pools from an industrial purification process, and the results were compared to those of the traditional approach of spiking model viruses and measuring their removal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Q‐PCR for measuring endogenous virus clearance by capture steps is a novel, alternative strategy that is applicable to at least one instance of virus clearance by chromatography.
the endogenous retrovirus in CHO cell culture can be used to evaluate virus removal by protein A chromatographic steps in a robust and cost effective manner.
